Historical acquisition errors are not treated as current-model residuals.","batch_rationale":"The batch supplies complementary labels for the retrained predictor. The m13 and m94 points resolve nonlinear endpoint curves around measured failures. Three m207 amounts at 2/1 test competing loading patterns directly, while two m116 measurements complete a two-ratio, two-amount experiment using existing observations. The m125 volume pair, its additional amount point, and the near-amount-matched m173 contrast test whether loading-solvent volume contains reproducible conditional information. These designs address recorded features the current forecasts often flatten, while acknowledging that unrecorded variation can remain. The m114 intermediate ratio and m159, m178 and m181 extensions probe carbonyl transfer without imposing a common retention shift. Nitrogen selections distinguish aminoaryl, secondary-amine, enamine-ester and quinoline environments. Paired m200 measurements extend donor learning beyond the heavily sampled methoxy alcohols. New m43, m68, m85 and m126 each receive two fixed-loading ratios so their labels can distinguish a scaffold offset from an incorrect solvent slope; these include moderate-retention neutral chemistry as well as difficult regions. One repeated m73 tuple tests the reproducibility of an anomalous response before it is generalized. Cross-scaffold comparisons retain their recorded loading differences and are not interpreted as isolated causal functional-group effects. Quantile widths are used only as ancillary model-spread signals, especially because some supplied quantiles cross. All 32 IDs and their supplied packet forecasts are fixed before any new label reveal. The intended benefit is better conditional V1/V2 prediction across the Row-distribution, through improved structural transfer, solvent curvature and loading representation."}
